sessions.description:
Session records associated with this guest.

Each session represents a temporary authentication window created when the guest registers via device fingerprint or refreshes their tokens. Every session captures audit metadata — IP address, current page URL, and referrer — along with explicit creation and expiration timestamps.

Sessions follow an append-only audit trail pattern: they are never modified or deleted once created. The array includes the current session (just created by the join or refresh operation) along with all historical sessions for the guest. Session validity is determined by comparing the `expired_at` field against the current time — expired sessions remain in the array for audit purposes.

Returns all session records for the guest as an array of IShoppingMallGuestSession. The newly created session from the current join or refresh operation is included alongside all previously created sessions. Sessions are append-only — never updated or deleted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was first created.

Records the exact moment the guest first accessed the platform and their device fingerprint was registered. This timestamp is set once at guest creation and remains immutable through all subsequent sessions and token refreshes. It helps distinguish first-time visitors from returning guests for audit and traffic analysis.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from shopping_mall_guests.created_at. ISO 8601 datetime with timezone (Timestamptz). Set once at guest creation and never mutated.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

Updated each time the guest establishes a new session — either through the join endpoint (initial registration or re-identification via device fingerprint) or the refresh endpoint (token renewal). This timestamp reflects the most recent activity and helps distinguish active guests from dormant ones for audit and cleanup purposes.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Sourced from shopping_mall_guests.updated_at. ISO 8601 datetime with timezone (Timestamptz). Updated each time the guest establishes a new session via join or refresh.

deleted_at.description:

Null for all active guest accounts. Set when the guest record is removed during periodic cleanup of inactive temporary accounts. In the authorization response context, this field is always null because soft-deleted guests are treated as not found — a new guest record with a fresh null `deleted_at` is created instead. Only guests with null `deleted_at` can successfully refresh their tokens.

In the authorization response, this is always null because: (1) soft-deleted guests are treated as not found during join, creating a fresh record; (2) only active guests with null deleted_at can successfully refresh tokens.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

IShoppingMallGuest.IAuthorized.description:
JWT token pair issued upon successful guest registration or token refresh.

The authorization response for unauthenticated visitors to the shopping mall platform. Combines three categories of data into a single response: the guest's identity information (unique identifier, device fingerprint, and account lifecycle timestamps), all session records associated with the guest (each capturing audit metadata including IP address, page URL, and referrer), and a JWT-based authorization token bundle for authenticating subsequent API requests.

This response is returned by both the join endpoint — where a guest first registers or is identified via device fingerprint — and the refresh endpoint — where an existing guest exchanges a valid refresh token for new tokens. Guest sessions follow an append-only audit trail pattern: each join or refresh creates a new session while preserving all previous sessions. The access token should be used as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. After the refresh token expires, the guest must re-establish identity through the join endpoint.
IShoppingMallGuest.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Computed JWT authorization response returned by both POST /auth/guest/join and POST /auth/guest/refresh. Guest identity fields (id, device_fingerprint, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are sourced from shopping_mall_guests. The sessions array is loaded via the one-to-many relation from shopping_mall_guests to shopping_mall_guest_sessions (JOIN on shopping_mall_guest_id), returning all session records for the guest as IShoppingMallGuestSession instances. The token property is computed entirely at response time: a JWT access token (15-min TTL, signed with server private key, claims: sub=guest.id, session_id=new_session.id), a JWT refresh token (24-hr TTL, same claims), access token expiration datetime (now + 15 minutes), and refreshable_until datetime (now + 24 hours). Tokens are cryptographically signed and never persisted in the database. Served by both POST /auth/guest/join (guest registration/identification) and POST /auth/guest/refresh (token renewal).

name.description:
Short, human-readable label identifying the category.

Used in product listings, search filters, and navigation throughout the platform. Category names help sellers decide where to list their products and help customers understand the category's scope. Examples include "Electronics", "Clothing", or "Home & Garden".

When updating, the new name must be unique within its parent scope. For top-level categories, the name must not conflict with any other top-level category. For subcategories, the name must not conflict with any other subcategory under the same parent.

Must be non-empty when present (whitespace-only strings are rejected at the service layer with HTTP 400). Name uniqueness is enforced within the target parent scope at the service layer (not schema level): two top-level categories cannot share the same name, and two subcategories under the same parent cannot share the same name. If the provided name matches an existing category within the same scope, the service returns HTTP 409.

Contextual explanation of what types of products belong in this category.

Guides sellers in placing products correctly and helps customers understand what they can expect to find within the category. This is a plain text field without formatting or markup.

When updating, the provided description replaces the current value entirely. There is no partial text update or append behavior — the full description text must be provided.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_categories.description. parentId.description:
Reference to the parent category for the platform's one-level nesting hierarchy.

Set to `null` to make this a top-level category with no parent. Provide a valid top-level category's UUID to place this category as a subcategory under that parent. The platform supports at most one level of nesting — a subcategory cannot itself become a parent to further subcategories.

A category cannot be its own parent, and circular reference chains are rejected at the service layer. The referenced parent category must exist and be active (not soft-deleted).

- Parent existence: the referenced category must exist and not be soft-deleted (HTTP 404 otherwise)
- Two-tier hierarchy: the parent must itself be a top-level category — subcategories cannot be parents (HTTP 400 otherwise)

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing product category.

All fields are optional — only the fields provided in the request are modified. Fields omitted from the request retain their current values. Administrators use this endpoint to edit category names and descriptions, reassign parent categories, or promote a subcategory to a top-level category by setting `parentId` to `null`.

The platform enforces a two-tier category hierarchy: a subcategory cannot become a parent to further subcategories, and no category may reference itself as its own parent either directly or through a chain. Category names must remain unique within their parent scope — two top-level categories cannot share the same name, and two subcategories under the same parent cannot share the same name.

Only authenticated administrators may perform this operation. Soft-deleted categories cannot be edited and must be restored before modification.

Maps to shopping_mall_categories table for partial updates. All three fields (name, description, parent_id) are optional — only the properties provided in the request body are applied; omitted fields retain their current values in the database. The target category is identified by the `categoryId` path parameter (maps to `id` column).

Service-layer validations (not encoded in schema):
- `name` must be non-empty when provided (whitespace-only rejected with 400)
- `name` must be unique within the target parent scope (409 on conflict)
- `parentId` must reference an existing active top-level category (404 if missing/deleted, 400 if parent is itself a subcategory)
- Circular reference detection: `parentId` must not equal the category's own ID or create a cycle
- Soft-deleted categories cannot be edited

`updated_at` is set server-side to the current timestamp on every successful update.

parentId.description:

When set to a UUID, returns only subcategories directly under that parent. When explicitly null, returns only top-level categories (those with no parent). When omitted entirely, returns all categories regardless of nesting level. The shopping_mall_category_id classifies the product for customer browsing and must reference an existing, active category. The base_price serves as the default price when variants have no price override.

This means browsing a parent category like "Electronics" returns products from "Electronics" itself plus products from all its subcategories like "Laptops" and "Tablets".

max_price.description:
Maximum price filter for narrowing results to products below a price threshold.

Only products with a base price less than or equal to this value are included in results. The filter applies to the product's base price, not individual variant prices.

in_stock_only.description:

When enabled, products whose all variants have zero or negative stock are excluded. Stock is computed from the inventory ledger by summing all quantity changes — a variant is considered in stock when its total quantity change is greater than zero.

Products that have no variants at all are always excluded when this filter is active. When disabled or omitted, both in-stock and out-of-stock products are included in results.

When false or absent, skip the filter — both in-stock and out-of-stock products are returned. Products without any variants are always excluded when this filter is active, since they have no inventory ledger.

- **price_asc**: Products are sorted by price from lowest to highest, helping customers find affordable options.
- **price_desc**: Products are sorted by price from highest to lowest, helping customers browse premium products.

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for browsing products across the platform catalog.

Provides the unified query interface for three customer-facing endpoints: category browsing, full catalog listing, and text-based product search. Every field is optional — when no criteria are specified, the endpoint returns all visible products sorted by newest first with default pagination of 20 items per page.

Product Visibility: The service layer applies mandatory visibility filters before any user-requested criteria. Soft-deleted products, products from suspended sellers, and products from banned sellers are always excluded regardless of the request parameters.

Text Search: The search field supports trigram-based fuzzy matching on product names, allowing customers to find products with partial or approximate search terms. When omitted, all visible products matching other criteria are returned.

Category Filtering: When a category ID is provided, products from that category and all its direct subcategories are automatically included. This enables browsing a parent category and seeing all products in its subtree without separate queries. When omitted, no category restriction is applied.

Price Range: Both minimum and maximum price filters apply to the product's base price. When both are specified, only products with prices between the two bounds are returned. Either filter can be used independently.

In-Stock Filtering: When enabled, only products with at least one variant having positive stock are returned. Stock is computed from the ledger-based inventory system by summing all quantity changes. Products without any variants are always excluded when this filter is active.

Sorting: Results can be ordered by newest first, lowest price first, or highest price first. When variants have price overrides, the effective price (variant override or base price) is used for price-based sorting.

Pagination: Offset-based pagination with a configurable page size between 1 and 100 items. The first page is page 1.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product optimized for list displays in search results and category browsing pages.

Contains essential product identification fields including the unique ID and display name. The thumbnail image provides the main product image — the first image by display order, or null when no images exist. Price information includes the base price as the default price, plus the minimum and maximum variant effective prices showing the price range across all non-deleted variants. When all variants share the same effective price or only one variant exists, both min and max equal that value; when no variants exist, both are null.

The seller provides the shop identity via a seller summary, allowing customers to see which shop offers the product. Customer feedback is represented by the average rating (null when no reviews exist, indicating "no rating") and the review count (total number of non-deleted reviews). The purchasable flag indicates whether the product has at least one variant with positive stock — products without purchasable variants are displayed as unavailable.
IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.x-autobe-specification:
Summary view of shopping_mall_products optimized for list displays.

Direct column mappings: id, name, base_price, created_at.

Computed properties:
- thumbnail_image_url: LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_product_images, first by display_order ASC WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, returns url or null.
- min_variant_price: MIN(effective_price) from non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants, where effective_price = variant.price_override ?? base_price. Null when no variants.
- max_variant_price: MAX(effective_price) from non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants. Null when no variants.
- average_rating: AVG(rating) from non-deleted shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE product_id = shopping_mall_products.id. Null when no reviews.
- review_count: COUNT(*) from non-deleted shopping_mall_review_reviews WHERE product_id = shopping_mall_products.id.
- is_purchasable: EXISTS non-deleted variant with SUM(shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change) > 0.

Excluded: description (large text), updated_at/deleted_at (system timestamps not needed in summary), shopping_mall_seller_id (FK replaced by seller $ref), shopping_mall_category_id/category (not required in summary listings per design spec), all HAS-MANY relations (images → thumbnail_image_url, variants → price range, reviews → rating/count, productSnapshots/wishlistItems/orderItemProductSnapshots → separate endpoints).

The category that classifies this product.

Every product belongs to exactly one category, which organizes products for customer browsing and search filtering. Categories may be top-level or subcategories within the platform's two-tier hierarchy.

The category summary includes the category's name, description, parent category reference, and subcategory count, providing enough context for breadcrumb navigation and category-based filtering. The category is included even if it has been soft-deleted, preserving the product's original classification.

seller.description:
The seller's storefront profile.

Identifies the seller who created and owns this product. The profile includes the seller's shop name, shop description, and logo image URI — the public-facing identity that customers see on product pages and in search results.

Gallery images belonging to this product, ordered by display position.

Each product can have multiple images forming a visual gallery that customers browse on the product detail page. The first image — the one with the lowest display order value — serves as the main thumbnail and is used in search results, category listings, and product cards.

variants.description:
Purchasable variants of this product, each with pricing and stock status.

Every variant represents a specific combination of option values — for example, a clothing product might have variants for 'Red / Small', 'Red / Large', 'Blue / Small', and 'Blue / Large'. Each variant carries a globally unique SKU code for inventory management and order processing.

Pricing for each variant includes both the variant's own price (if an override is set) and the product's base price for comparison. The effective purchase price is the variant's price when set, or the base price when not.

Stock quantity is computed dynamically by summing all inventory ledger entries — a positive value means the variant is in stock and available for purchase. A value of zero or less means the variant is out of stock. Products with no variants at all are displayed as unavailable for purchase.

For each variant: include optionValues from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values (key-value pairs), compute stock_quantity as SUM of all shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change for the variant, include base_price from the parent product. When a variant has no price override (price IS NULL), the effective purchase price is base_price. Returns IShoppingMallProductVariant.

reviews.description:
Customer reviews for this product, sorted newest first.

Each review includes a star rating from 1 to 5, optional written feedback, and the reviewer's identity. Reviews are written by verified purchasers after their order item reaches delivered status. A customer may write one review per product per order — purchasing the same product across multiple orders allows separate reviews.

Reviews from customers who have deleted their accounts are preserved but the author is shown as 'deleted user' rather than exposing the original display name. Soft-deleted reviews are excluded entirely from this list and from the average rating calculation.

The list is sorted with the most recent reviews first, ensuring customers see the freshest feedback at the top of the page.

When the authoring customer's deleted_at IS NOT NULL, display author as 'deleted user' rather than the original display_name. Returns IShoppingMallReviewReview.ISummary.

Calculated as the arithmetic mean of all non-deleted review ratings. A value of null means the product has not yet received any reviews — this is distinct from a low numeric rating and should be displayed to customers as 'no rating' rather than a numerical score.

When reviews exist, the average is a number typically between 1.0 and 5.0. Soft-deleted reviews are excluded from the calculation, so the average reflects only currently visible feedback.

Returns null — not zero — when no non-deleted reviews exist, distinguishing 'no rating yet' from 'rated zero stars'. The average is recalculated on every read; no caching is assumed at the schema level.

review_count.description:
Total number of customer reviews for this product.

Shows how many customers have reviewed this product, helping shoppers gauge the reliability of the average rating. A higher review count means the average rating is based on more opinions and is therefore more trustworthy.

Only non-deleted reviews are counted. The count includes all reviews regardless of rating value — a product with one 5-star review and a product with one 1-star review both show a count of 1.

Timestamp when the product was first created.

Instead, this timestamp is set and the product becomes invisible to customers — it no longer appears in search results or category listings and is removed from all customer wishlists. IShoppingMallProduct.description:

Aggregates everything a customer needs to evaluate a single product: the product's core identity (name, description, category, and base price), the seller's storefront profile, all gallery images in their display order, every purchasable variant with its SKU code, option attributes, pricing, and live stock status, and all customer reviews sorted newest first along with the calculated average rating and total review count.

The product detail page is the destination after a customer clicks on a product from search results or category listings. This DTO provides the full depth of information that the summary view intentionally omits — the complete description text, the full image gallery, all variant options and stock levels, and the entire review history.

Products with no variants are displayed as unavailable for purchase but remain visible so customers can see the product exists. Products from suspended sellers are hidden from customers but remain accessible to the owning seller and platform administrators. Soft-deleted products return 404 for customers and non-owning sellers.

Represents an immutable snapshot of a product variant's complete state at a specific point in time.

Variant snapshots are created automatically whenever a product variant is edited, preserving the variant's SKU code, option values, price, and stock quantity exactly as they existed before the change took effect. Snapshots are also created as children of product snapshots when the parent product is modified, enabling reconstruction of the full product-variant configuration at any historical point.

A null shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id indicates a standalone variant snapshot created from a variant-only edit (where a seller modified the variant without changing the parent product). A non-null value indicates the snapshot was created as part of a product-level edit and is linked to its parent product snapshot.

Snapshots are permanently immutable — they can never be modified or deleted by any actor, including sellers, customers, administrators, and super administrators. Snapshots are preserved indefinitely even after the parent variant, product, or category is deleted, providing an unalterable audit trail for dispute resolution and historical reference.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing product variant owned by the authenticated seller.

Allows the seller to modify a variant's SKU code, option values, and price override. All fields are optional — only the fields provided are updated, and omitted fields retain their current values.

**SKU Code**: When changed, the new code must be globally unique across all variants on the platform. The system validates against every existing variant's code and rejects duplicates with a conflict error.

**Option Values**: When provided, the new set completely replaces the existing option values. Each key within the variant must be unique. This is a full replacement, not a partial update — all existing option values are removed and the new set is inserted in a single transaction.

**Price Override**: When set to a positive number, it overrides the parent product's base price for purchases of this variant. When set to null, the override is removed and the product's base price applies.

**Stock Quantity**: Managed exclusively through inventory records and is not editable through this endpoint. Use the inventory management endpoints to record stock changes.

The total price is frozen at checkout and never recalculated, preserving the actual amount the customer paid regardless of later price changes. The overall order status is derived from the statuses of its constituent order items — "paid" when all items are paid, "shipped" when any item ships, "delivered" when all items are delivered, "cancelled" when all items are cancelled, "refunded" when all items are refunded, or "partially_completed" when items are in mixed states.

**Order Items**: Each item in the items array represents a purchased product variant with quantity, unit price frozen at purchase time, and its own independent lifecycle status. Product name, variant SKU code and option values, and seller shop name are all preserved via snapshots taken at the moment of purchase, guaranteeing historical accuracy regardless of later product or pricing changes.

**Shipments**: The shipments array lists all seller-created packages for this order, each with carrier name, tracking number, shipping date, and delivery confirmation status. Different sellers always ship separately, and a single seller may create multiple shipments. Each shipment maps to the order items it contains, showing which items traveled together.

Specifies the inclusive start of a date range for filtering by the shipment creation (shipping) date. Shipments with a created_at timestamp equal to or later than this value are included in results.

Use together with createdTo to define a complete date range.
createdFrom.x-autobe-specification:
Inclusive lower bound filter on created_at column of shopping_mall_shipments.

Applied as: WHERE created_at >= :createdFrom.

Can be used independently (without createdTo) to find all shipments created on or after a specific date. Used together with createdTo to define a complete date range.

createdTo.description:
Filter shipments created on or before this date and time.

Specifies the inclusive end of a date range for filtering by the shipment creation (shipping) date. Shipments with a created_at timestamp equal to or earlier than this value are included in results.

Use together with createdFrom to define a complete date range.
createdTo.x-autobe-specification:
Inclusive upper bound filter on created_at column of shopping_mall_shipments.

Applied as: WHERE created_at <= :createdTo.

Can be used independently (without createdFrom) to find all shipments created on or before a specific date. Used together with createdFrom to define a complete date range.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of shipment records to return per page when using cursor-based pagination.

Controls the page size for cursor-navigated result sets. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Defaults to 20 records per page when omitted.

Use together with cursor for efficient traversal of large result sets without offset-based performance degradation. Cursor-based pagination provides stable results even when new shipments are created between requests.
pageSize.x-autobe-specification:
Cursor-based pagination: maximum number of records per page. Applied as LIMIT in the SQL query.

Default value: 20. Maximum allowed: 100.

Primary pagination mechanism for shipment listings. The cursor parameter (returned in response pagination metadata) is used to navigate to the next page. Cursor-based pagination provides stable traversal unaffected by concurrent inserts.

cursor.description:
Opaque cursor token for navigating paginated shipment results.

Pass the cursor value from a previous response's pagination metadata to retrieve the next page of results. When omitted or null, the first page is returned.

Cursor-based pagination provides stable result traversal that is not affected by new shipments being created between requests.
cursor.x-autobe-specification:
Opaque cursor token for cursor-based pagination. Obtained from the pagination metadata of a previous response.

When provided, the query returns results after the cursor position. When null or omitted, results start from the beginning (first page).

The cursor encodes the last record's sort position (created_at DESC, id) to enable stable, efficient keyset pagination even as new records are inserted.

page.description:
Target page number for offset-based pagination.

Specifies which page of results to return using 1-based indexing. Page 1 is the first page. Defaults to page 1 when omitted or null.

Requesting a page beyond the available range returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata reflecting actual totals. For better performance on large result sets, consider using cursor-based pagination (pageSize and cursor) instead.
page.x-autobe-specification:
Offset-based pagination: 1-indexed page number. Applied as OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit in the SQL query.

Defaults to 1 (first page) when null or omitted.

Secondary pagination mechanism alongside limit. For most use cases, cursor-based pagination (pageSize + cursor) is preferred for better performance and stability on large result sets.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipment records to return per page when using offset-based pagination.

Controls how many records appear in each page when navigating with the page parameter. Defaults to 100 records per page when omitted.

The actual number of records returned may be fewer on the last page or when total matching records are below this threshold.
limit.x-autobe-specification:
Offset-based pagination: maximum number of records per page. Applied as LIMIT in the SQL query.

Defaults to 100 when null or omitted.

Works together with page for offset-based navigation. The actual number of records returned may be fewer on the last page or when total matching records are below this threshold.

IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing shipments.

Provides optional filters for narrowing shipment results by delivery status, order reference, seller reference, and shipping date range. All filters are optional and can be combined — an empty request body returns all scoped shipments sorted newest first.

Pagination is supported through both cursor-based (pageSize, cursor) and offset-based (page, limit) mechanisms for flexible client integration. Cursor-based pagination is preferred for stable traversal of large result sets.
IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter and pagination parameters for listing shipments from shopping_mall_shipments.

Filters (all optional, combinable):
- deliveryStatus: derived from delivered_at column. "pending" → WHERE delivered_at IS NULL. "delivered" → WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL.
- orderId: exact match on shopping_mall_order_id column. Redundant in order-scoped endpoints (/orders/{orderId}/shipments) but accepted for API uniformity.
- sellerId: exact match on shopping_mall_seller_id column. Authorization middleware must reject with 403 for customer and seller roles — only valid for administrators.
- createdFrom: inclusive lower bound on created_at column (WHERE created_at >= :createdFrom).
- createdTo: inclusive upper bound on created_at column (WHERE created_at <= :createdTo).

Pagination (dual mechanism):
- Cursor-based: pageSize (default 20, max 100) and cursor (opaque token from previous response). Preferred for stable traversal.
- Offset-based: page (1-indexed, default 1) and limit (default 100). OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit, applied as LIMIT.

Default sort: created_at DESC (newest shipments first).

Authorization scoping (applied by endpoint middleware, not this DTO):
- Customer: auto-scoped to shipments where order's shopping_mall_customer_id matches authenticated user.
- Seller: auto-scoped to shipments where shopping_mall_seller_id matches authenticated seller.
- Admin: no automatic scoping.

items.description:
The product variants to purchase in this order.

Each entry identifies a specific variant by its unique ID and the desired quantity. The system validates stock availability for every requested variant before processing. On successful payment, each entry becomes an individual order item with its own lifecycle status, starting as "paid".

At least one item is required. Multiple items may span different sellers — each seller's items are managed independently through shipping, cancellation, and refund workflows.
items.x-autobe-specification: Array of IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate entries, each specifying a product variant by variant_id and a desired quantity (positive integer). On successful payment, the system atomically: (1) creates a shopping_mall_order_items row per entry with status 'paid', frozen unit price from the variant's current price, and quantity; (2) captures product, variant, and seller snapshots for each item; (3) deducts inventory via negative inventory_records; (4) removes matching cart_items. At least one item is required (minItems: 1). Variant IDs are validated server-side — the variant must exist, not be soft-deleted, and have sufficient stock.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description:
Request body for placing a new order.

Contains the items to purchase and the complete shipping destination. Each item specifies a product variant by ID and the desired quantity. At least one item is required.

All shipping address fields are required and frozen at order creation — they cannot be changed after the order is placed. The total price is computed server-side from current variant prices and must not be submitted by the client.
IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps to shopping_mall_orders table for order creation. The items array drives creation of shopping_mall_order_items rows after payment processing. Shipping address fields (recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country) are denormalized into the order at creation and frozen immutably. Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID primary key), code (server-generated unique order number), shopping_mall_customer_id (resolved from customer JWT session), total_price (server-computed from current variant prices — never trust client), status (always 'paid' on creation), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps). Relations excluded: customer (BELONGS-TO, FK from JWT), orderItems (HAS-MANY, created atomically from items array during transaction), shipments (HAS-MANY, created later by seller), reviews (HAS-MANY, created later by customer).

IShoppingMallOrderItemSellerSnapshot.description:
Immutable seller profile snapshot captured at the moment of order creation.

Preserves the seller's shop name and logo image as they appeared when an order was placed. This ensures historical accuracy — even if the seller later changes their profile or deletes their account, past orders continue to display the original seller information. Each snapshot belongs to exactly one order item and is created automatically during checkout, never modified afterward.

logo_image_url may be null if the seller had not uploaded a logo image at the time of purchase.

Returns all columns: id, shop_name, logo_image_url (nullable), and created_at. The shopping_mall_order_item_id FK column and orderItem relation are excluded — the parent order item context is provided by the {itemId} path parameter. The table has @@unique([shopping_mall_order_item_id]), so exactly zero or one row matches. Return 404 if no snapshot exists. The snapshot is immutable; no write operations are needed.

status.description:
The seller's decision on the cancellation request.

Must be either "approved" to accept the cancellation or "rejected" to decline it. An approved decision cancels the associated order item, processes a refund for that item, and restores the product variant's stock quantity. A rejected decision leaves the order item in its current "paid" status, allowing the customer to submit a new cancellation request for the same item later.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.status. Only valid values are 'approved' or 'rejected'. On 'approved': system cancels order item, processes refund, restores variant stock via positive inventory record equal to order item quantity, creates cancellation_request_snapshot. On 'rejected': order item remains 'paid', customer may re-request, snapshot still created. All operations atomic.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IUpdate.description:
The seller's decision on a pending cancellation request.

Contains the new status for the cancellation request being reviewed by the seller. Set to "approved" to accept the cancellation — this cancels the order item, processes a refund, and restores the variant's stock quantity through a positive inventory record.

Set to "rejected" to decline the cancellation — the order item remains in its current "paid" state, and the customer may submit a new cancellation request for the same item later. On either decision, the system creates an immutable snapshot preserving the request state at the moment of response for audit and dispute resolution.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Seller response payload for a pending cancellation request identified by {requestId} path parameter. Only status is mutable — accepts 'approved' (cancels order item, processes refund, restores stock via inventory record) or 'rejected' (order item remains 'paid', customer may re-request). System creates an immutable cancellation_request_snapshot on response. On approval: order item transitions to 'cancelled', variant stock restored via positive inventory record equal to order item quantity. All operations (status update, snapshot creation, inventory record creation, order item status change) must be atomic.

reason.description:
The customer's explanation for requesting a refund.

This free-text field captures the customer's justification — for example, product defect, item not as described, changed mind after receiving the item, or any other reason the customer wishes to communicate to the seller. The reason is visible to the seller when reviewing the request and is preserved immutably for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

The reason must be a non-empty string and cannot consist solely of whitespace characters. It is permanently recorded and carried into refund request snapshots when the seller responds.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from refund_requests.reason. Customer-provided free-text explanation for requesting the refund. Validated on the server: must be present, non-empty, and not whitespace-only. Preserved immutably — once the request is created, the reason cannot be changed. Stored in the refund_requests table and captured in snapshots when the seller responds.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a refund request on a delivered order item.

The customer provides a reason explaining why the refund is sought. This reason is preserved immutably and is visible to the seller when reviewing the request. The reason must be a non-empty string and cannot consist solely of whitespace characters.
IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: ICreate DTO for refund request submission. Only the customer-provided reason is accepted in the request body. All other fields are server-managed: id is auto-generated UUID, shopping_mall_order_item_id is resolved from the {itemId} path parameter, status is auto-set to 'pending', responded_at is auto-set to null, created_at and updated_at are auto-timestamps, and deleted_at is auto-set to null. The orderItem relation is resolved server-side via the path parameter FK chain. The snapshots has-many relation is created later when the seller responds — not part of creation.

search.description:
Free-text search term for finding refund requests by keywords in the customer's reason.

Searches against the customer-provided explanation text using fuzzy text matching. Useful for finding requests by specific product names, defect descriptions, or other keywords the customer included in their refund justification.

When a search term is provided, results are ordered by relevance rather than chronological order. When omitted, results default to newest-first ordering.
search.x-autobe-specification: Free-text search against the reason column in shopping_mall_refund_requests using PostgreSQL trigram similarity (pg_trgm). Leverages the GIN index on reason for efficient fuzzy matching. When a search term is provided, results are ordered by relevance (similarity score descending). When omitted or empty, results follow default newest-first ordering by created_at descending.

status.description:
Filter refund requests by their current approval workflow status.

Refund requests progress through three statuses in the seller review workflow:

- **pending**: The request is awaiting the seller's review and decision. No action has been taken yet.
- **approved**: The seller has accepted the refund. Refund processing and stock restoration are triggered.
- **rejected**: The seller has declined the refund. No further action is taken, though the customer may submit a new request within the remaining 7-day window.

When this filter is omitted, requests of all statuses are included in the results.
status.x-autobe-specification: Filter by single status value against the status column in shopping_mall_refund_requests. Must be one of: "pending" (awaiting seller review — initial state on creation), "approved" (seller accepted the refund — triggers refund processing and stock restoration), or "rejected" (seller declined the refund — no further action taken). When omitted, all statuses are included.

created_from.description:
Start of the date range for filtering by request submission time (inclusive).

Filters refund requests to those submitted on or after this datetime. Must be used together with created_to to form a complete date range — providing only one endpoint has no effect.

Use this to find requests submitted within a specific time window, such as "all requests from the last 7 days" or "all requests submitted this month."
created_from.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound for date range filter on created_at (request submission timestamp) in shopping_mall_refund_requests. Must be used together with created_to — providing only one endpoint has no filtering effect. Both values must be valid ISO 8601 datetime strings.

created_to.description:
End of the date range for filtering by request submission time (inclusive).

Filters refund requests to those submitted on or before this datetime. Must be used together with created_from to form a complete date range — providing only one endpoint has no effect.

Use this together with created_from to define a submission time window for browsing requests from a specific period.
created_to.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound for date range filter on created_at (request submission timestamp) in shopping_mall_refund_requests. Must be used together with created_from — providing only one endpoint has no filtering effect. Both values must be valid ISO 8601 datetime strings.

responded_from.description:
Start of the date range for filtering by seller response time (inclusive).

Filters refund requests to those where the seller responded on or after this datetime. Must be used together with responded_to to form a complete date range.

This filter is only meaningful for non-pending requests — pending requests have no response timestamp and will be excluded regardless of the date range. Use this to find requests resolved within a specific period, such as "all approved requests from this week."
responded_from.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound for date range filter on responded_at (seller response timestamp) in shopping_mall_refund_requests. Must be used together with responded_to — providing only one endpoint has no filtering effect. Only meaningful for requests where status is not "pending" (responded_at is populated). Both values must be valid ISO 8601 datetime strings.

responded_to.description:
End of the date range for filtering by seller response time (inclusive).

Filters refund requests to those where the seller responded on or before this datetime. Must be used together with responded_from to form a complete date range.

This filter is only meaningful for non-pending requests. Use this together with responded_from to define a response time window for reviewing how quickly sellers handle refund requests.
responded_to.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound for date range filter on responded_at (seller response timestamp) in shopping_mall_refund_requests. Must be used together with responded_from — providing only one endpoint has no filtering effect. Only meaningful for requests where status is not "pending" (responded_at is populated). Both values must be valid ISO 8601 datetime strings.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results (1-indexed).

Controls which page of matching refund requests is returned. Page numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1. Combined with limit, this determines the offset into the full result set.

Defaults to 1 (first page) when omitted. Pages beyond the available range return an empty data array.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund request records per page.

Controls the page size for paginated results. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Larger values return more records per page but increase response size and query time.

The actual number of records in the response may be less than this value on the final page or when total matching records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records to return per page. Clamped between 1 and 100 inclusive. Used as SQL LIMIT in the paginated query. Defaults to a server-configured value (typically 20) when omitted.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for browsing refund request lists.

This request body supports three classes of query parameters: free-text search against the customer-provided refund reason, status-based filtering, and date range filters on both submission and response timestamps. Pagination controls determine result page size and offset.

**Filtering by status**

Refund requests progress through three states in the seller review workflow. Filter by "pending" to see requests awaiting seller action, "approved" to see accepted refunds where processing has completed, or "rejected" to see declined requests.

**Date range filtering**

Two independent date range pairs are available. The created_from/created_to pair filters by when the customer submitted the request. The responded_from/responded_to pair filters by when the seller responded — this pair is only meaningful for non-pending requests since pending requests have no response timestamp.

**Search behavior**

When a search term is provided, results are ordered by relevance against the reason text. Without search, results default to newest-first ordering. All filters combine additively — applying multiple criteria narrows results by all conditions simultaneously.
IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameters object for paginated refund request search against shopping_mall_refund_requests.

**Search and Filtering**:
- search: Free-text search against the reason column using PostgreSQL trigram similarity (leveraging GIN index). Results ordered by relevance when search is active, by created_at descending (newest first) when browsing without search.
- status: Filter by single status value — "pending" (awaiting seller review), "approved" (seller accepted the refund), or "rejected" (seller declined the refund).
- created_from / created_to: Inclusive date range filter on created_at (request submission timestamp). Both endpoints required together — providing only one has no effect.
- responded_from / responded_to: Inclusive date range filter on responded_at (seller response timestamp). Both endpoints required together. Only meaningful for non-pending requests where responded_at is populated.

**Pagination**:
- page: 1-indexed page number for offset-based pagination. Defaults to 1.
- limit: Maximum records per page, clamped between 1 and 100.

**Server-enforced behaviors (not in request schema)**:
- Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from results.
- Data ownership isolation enforced server-side based on authenticated actor:
  - Customer: JOIN through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_orders, filter by shopping_mall_customer_id matching auth actor.
  - Seller: JOIN through shopping_mall_order_items → shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products, filter by seller's ID.
  - Admin: No ownership filter — views all refund requests across the platform.
- Default sort: created_at descending (newest first).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart item.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key for this cart entry. This identifier is globally unique across all customers and is used to reference the item in update and delete operations.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cart_items.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on cart item creation.

customer.description:
The customer who owns this cart item.

Contains the essential summary fields of the authenticated customer: their unique identifier, login email address, public display name, registration timestamp, and optional ban status. This relation is resolved via a JOIN on the shopping_mall_customer_id foreign key. Cart items are strictly scoped to the owning customer — the system verifies ownership on all read and update operations.
customer.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation. JOIN shopping_mall_customers ON shopping_mall_customer_id = customers.id. Returns IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary with id, email, display_name, created_at, and banned_at.

productVariant.description:
The product variant (SKU) the customer has added to the cart.

Contains the variant's globally unique SKU code, its option values (e.g., color and size), the effective price (variant-specific override or the parent product's base price), and the current stock quantity derived from inventory records. This is the specific purchasable unit — customers must select a variant, not just a product. The variant's availability status at checkout time is reflected in the computed available flag on the cart item.
productVariant.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation. JOIN shopping_mall_product_variants ON shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variants.id. Returns IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary with id, code, optionValues, price, stock_quantity, created_at, and updated_at. Stock is derived from SUM of inventory records; optionValues from LEFT JOIN on option_values table.

quantity.description:
The number of units of the product variant the customer wants to purchase.

Must be a positive integer of 1 or greater. When the customer adds the same variant to the cart again, this quantity is incremented rather than creating a separate cart entry. The quantity can be updated at any time before checkout. If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, the computed available flag will be false to warn the customer.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cart_items.quantity. Must be a positive integer (≥ 1). When the same variant is added again, the quantity is incremented rather than creating a duplicate entry — enforced by the unique constraint on (customer_id, product_variant_id).

available.description:
Whether this cart item can proceed to checkout.

Computed at query time based on the current state of the referenced product variant. Returns true only when both conditions are met: the variant has not been soft-deleted by the seller, and the variant has sufficient stock to cover the requested quantity. When false, the productVariant reference can be inspected to determine the specific reason — either the variant was removed, or the available stock is insufficient. The cart item itself persists regardless of availability so the customer can see the affected item and take corrective action.
available.x-autobe-specification: Computed field — NOT stored in the database. Derived at query time with two conditions: (1) the referenced shopping_mall_product_variant must have deleted_at IS NULL (variant not soft-deleted), and (2) the SUM of all shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity for the variant must be ≥ this cart item's quantity (sufficient stock). Returns false if either condition fails. The cart item record itself is never modified — this is a read-time derivation only.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item was first created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format. This value is set once when the customer first adds the product variant to their cart and does not change on subsequent quantity updates.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cart_items.created_at. Set to the current timestamp when the cart item is first inserted. Immutable after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item was last modified.

Recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format. Updated each time the quantity changes — whether through an explicit quantity update or when the same variant is added again and the quantities are combined. This allows the frontend to sort or highlight recently modified cart entries.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_cart_items.updated_at. Refreshed to the current timestamp on every quantity change, including when the same variant is added again (quantity incremented).

IShoppingMallCartItem.description:
Complete representation of a single shopping cart entry with enriched product variant and customer details.

Each cart item links an authenticated customer to a specific product variant (SKU) with a desired purchase quantity. The product variant reference is resolved to include the SKU code, option values, effective price (variant override or parent product base price), current stock quantity, and parent product metadata — providing all information needed for immediate cart UI rendering without additional API calls.

The available flag is a query-time computation reflecting whether the item can be checked out. It is true when the referenced variant has not been soft-deleted and has sufficient inventory to cover the requested quantity. When false, the client should inspect the productVariant reference to surface the specific reason to the customer — either the variant was removed by the seller, or stock is insufficient for the desired quantity.
IShoppingMallCartItem.x-autobe-specification: Direct columns: id, quantity, created_at, updated_at from shopping_mall_cart_items. 2. order_items_count: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_order_items WHERE shopping_mall_product_variant_id IN (SELECT pv.id FROM shopping_mall_product_variants pv JOIN shopping_mall_products p ON pv.shopping_mall_product_id = p.id WHERE p.shopping_mall_seller_id = <authenticatedSellerId> AND p.deleted_at IS NULL).

3. pending_cancellations_count: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_cancellation_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND deleted_at IS NULL AND shopping_mall_order_item_id IN (same order item subquery as step 2).

4. pending_refunds_count: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_refund_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND deleted_at IS NULL AND shopping_mall_order_item_id IN (same order item subquery as step 2).

Edge cases: If the authenticated seller has no products, all four counts return 0. Soft-deleted products, cancellation requests, and refund requests are excluded from all counts. Only approved sellers can access this endpoint (enforced at the operation level, not the schema level). Pure read operation with no side effects.

The page number to retrieve for offset-based pagination.

Page numbering is 1-indexed — the first page is page 1, not page 0. When combined with limit, the server computes the SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) × limit to skip records from previous pages.

This field is ignored when cursor-based pagination is active via the cursor parameter. Cursor-based pagination is preferred for large datasets as it avoids the performance degradation of deep offsets.

The actual number of records returned may be fewer than the limit on the last page or when total matching records are fewer than the requested limit.

cursor.description:
A cursor value for cursor-based pagination, enabling stable and efficient traversal of large result sets.

When provided, the server switches from offset-based to cursor-based pagination: it returns records positioned after this cursor based on the current sort field and direction. For descending sort (the default: newest first), the query filters WHERE sortField < cursor. For ascending sort, WHERE sortField > cursor.

Cursor-based pagination is recommended for large review datasets as it maintains consistent performance regardless of page depth, unlike offset-based pagination which degrades with higher page numbers.

Applied as WHERE {sortField} < cursor (for DESC sort) or WHERE {sortField} > cursor (for ASC sort), combined with LIMIT {limit}. When this field is provided, offset-based pagination (page) is ignored. Not mapped to any database column — purely a query-layer parameter.

- **created_at** (default): Order reviews by their original submission date. This is the default and matches the product detail page display where newest reviews appear first.
- **rating**: Order reviews by star rating. Combined with ascending direction, this groups critical reviews (low ratings) first; with descending, it surfaces the most positive reviews.
- **updated_at**: Order reviews by their most recent modification timestamp — including edits, rating changes, and soft-deletions. Useful for finding recently modified reviews.

- 'rating' → shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating (integer, star rating 1-5)
- 'updated_at' → shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at (timestamptz, last modification timestamp)

The sort direction is controlled by sortDirection. Defaults to 'created_at' when not specified.

sortDirection.description:
The direction to sort results.

- **desc** (default): Descending order — newest reviews first, highest ratings first, most recently updated first. This matches the product detail page display where customers expect to see the most recent feedback at the top.
- **asc**: Ascending order — oldest reviews first, lowest ratings first, least recently updated first. Useful for chronological browsing or auditing review histories.

A free-text search term to find reviews containing specific words or phrases in their written feedback.

Performs a case-insensitive partial match against the review's optional written content. For example, searching for "quality" returns all reviews whose content contains the word "quality" anywhere in the text, regardless of capitalization.

Reviews that consist solely of a star rating with no written content are never matched by this filter. The search supports natural language phrases — multi-word terms match reviews containing those words in sequence.

IShoppingMallReviewReview.IRequest.description:

**Sorting and pagination**: Results are sorted newest first by default, matching the display order on product detail pages. Alternative sorting by star rating or last-modified date is supported.
