**Rating filters**:
- When `rating` is provided (used by product-specific endpoint PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/reviews): WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating = [value]
- When `ratingMin` and/or `ratingMax` are provided (used by global search endpoint PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/reviews): WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating >= ratingMin AND shopping_mall_review_reviews.rating <= ratingMax
- Both bounds are inclusive. The rating column is a non-null integer constrained to 1-5 at the application layer.

**Date range filters**:
- createdFrom/createdTo → WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at >= createdFrom AND shopping_mall_review_reviews.created_at <= createdTo
- updatedFrom/updatedTo → WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at >= updatedFrom AND shopping_mall_review_reviews.updated_at <= updatedTo
- Both bounds are inclusive. Uses timestamptz columns.

**Content search**: contentSearch → WHERE shopping_mall_review_reviews.content ILIKE '%' || contentSearch || '%' (case-insensitive partial match). Reviews with NULL content are never matched. Leverages the PostgreSQL trigram index on the content column when available.

**Sorting**: ORDER BY {sortField} {sortDirection}:
- sortField maps to shopping_mall_review_reviews columns: 'created_at' → created_at, 'rating' → rating, 'updated_at' → updated_at
- sortDirection: 'asc' → ASC, 'desc' → DESC
- Default: created_at DESC (newest first), matching the product detail page display order and leveraging the index on (shopping_mall_product_id, created_at).

**Pagination — offset-based**: OFFSET (page - 1) * limit, LIMIT {limit}. When page is provided and cursor is not.
**Pagination — cursor-based**: WHERE {sortField} < cursor (for DESC) or > cursor (for ASC), LIMIT {limit}. When cursor is provided, page is ignored.
**Limit**: default 20, hard maximum 100.
**Total count**: Always compute COUNT(*) of the filtered result set (before LIMIT/OFFSET) to populate IPage.IPagination.records.

**All filters are combined conjunctively (AND).** All filter fields are optional — when none are provided, the query returns all non-deleted reviews sorted newest first.

**Access control** (enforced at the middleware/service layer, not in this DTO):
- Guests: denied entirely.
- Customers: may query their own reviews; customerId is resolved from JWT and overrides any user-supplied value.
- Sellers: may filter reviews for their own products; scoped at the service layer.
- Administrators: unrestricted access including the includeDeleted override.
- Non-admin requests with includeDeleted: true are rejected with 403 or silently overridden to false.

**Deleted user handling**: When a review's author has deleted their customer account, the review content and rating are preserved. The author attribution as 'deleted user' is handled in the ISummary response layer, not in the filtering logic. Deleted customers' reviews still appear in query results (they are not filtered out).

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
A single line item within a customer order, representing the purchase of a specific product variant with the quantity and unit price frozen at the moment of order creation.

Each order item has an independent lifecycle status — paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded — that progresses separately from other items in the same order. The price is captured once at purchase and never changes, ensuring historical accuracy regardless of later product or variant price adjustments.

The response includes purchase-time snapshots of the product, variant, and seller profile, preserving the exact context at the moment of purchase. This historical integrity is maintained even if the underlying products, variants, or seller profiles have since been modified, suspended, or deleted. If the item has been assigned to a shipment by the seller, the associated carrier name and tracking number are included. Any active cancellation or refund requests linked to this item are also returned.
IShoppingMallOrderItem.x-autobe-specification:
Direct columns from shopping_mall_order_items: id, quantity, price, status, created_at, updated_at.

BELONGS-TO relations (replacing FK columns with ISummary objects):
- order → IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary via shopping_mall_order_id JOIN on shopping_mall_orders (code, status, created_at)
- variant → IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary via shopping_mall_product_variant_id JOIN on shopping_mall_product_variants (id, code) with optionValues from shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values
- shipment → IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary | null via nullable shopping_mall_shipment_id JOIN on shopping_mall_shipments (carrier_name, tracking_number, delivered_at, created_at)

1:1 snapshot relations (all nullable per DB optional relations — handle missing gracefully):
- productSnapshot → IShoppingMallOrderItemProductSnapshot | null via shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots (join on shopping_mall_order_item_id unique)
- variantSnapshot → IShoppingMallOrderItemVariantSnapshot | null via shopping_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots (join on shopping_mall_order_item_id unique)
- sellerSnapshot → IShoppingMallOrderItemSellerSnapshot | null via shopping_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots (join on shopping_mall_order_item_id unique)

HAS-MANY collections:
- cancellationRequests → IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ISummary[] from shopping_mall_cancellation_requests where shopping_mall_order_item_id matches, filter deleted_at IS NULL
- refundRequests → IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ISummary[] from shopping_mall_refund_requests where shopping_mall_order_item_id matches, filter deleted_at IS NULL

IShoppingMallProduct.IDetail.description:
Comprehensive product detail page data aggregating product information, category, seller profile, image gallery, purchasable variants with stock status, customer reviews, and computed rating statistics.

This type is the response for the customer product detail endpoint. It combines product metadata with all related entities needed to render a complete product detail page.

Product fields include the name, description, and base price — the base price serves as the default, with individual variants potentially overriding it.

Relations include the product's category (name and identifier), the seller's shop profile (shop name and logo), the complete image gallery in display order, all available variants with their option values, prices, and current stock quantities, and all published reviews with reviewer attribution and computed aggregate rating.
IShoppingMallProduct.IDetail.x-autobe-specification: Primary: shopping_mall_products (id, name, description, base_price, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). JOIN shopping_mall_categories via shopping_mall_category_id for category ISummary (id, name). JOIN shopping_mall_seller_profiles via shopping_mall_seller_id for seller ISummary (shop_name, logo_image_uri). Load shopping_mall_product_images ordered by display_order ASC for images array. Load non-deleted shopping_mall_product_variants (deleted_at IS NULL) with child shopping_mall_product_variant_option_values for variants array; stock computed by summing shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change per variant. Load non-deleted shopping_mall_review_reviews (deleted_at IS NULL) ordered by created_at DESC for reviews array; JOIN shopping_mall_customers via shopping_mall_customer_id for reviewer display_name (show 'deleted user' if customer soft-deleted). Compute average_rating: mean of all non-deleted review ratings, rounded to 1 decimal, null if none. Compute review_count: count of non-deleted reviews. Compute is_available: true when product has at least one non-deleted variant.

variant_id.description:
The unique identifier of the product variant to purchase.

References a specific SKU variant from the product catalog. The variant must exist, not be soft-deleted, and have sufficient stock to fulfill the requested quantity.

Stock availability is validated server-side during checkout — if any variant is out of stock or has insufficient quantity, the entire order is rejected.
variant_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_product_variant_id. BELONGS-TO FK referencing shopping_mall_product_variants.id. The variant must exist, not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL), and have sufficient stock (derived from SUM of shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity for that variant). Stock validation is performed server-side during checkout — if any variant is out of stock or has insufficient quantity, the entire order is rejected.

quantity.description:
The number of units of this variant to purchase.

Must be a positive integer of at least 1. When the same variant is added to the cart multiple times, quantities combine into a single order item at checkout rather than creating separate line items.

The system validates that the requested quantity does not exceed available stock. If the requested quantity exceeds the current stock level for the variant, the entire order is rejected.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to shopping_mall_order_items.quantity. Must be a positive integer of at least 1. When the same variant is added to the cart multiple times, quantities combine into a single order item at checkout rather than creating separate line items. The system validates that the requested quantity does not exceed available stock (derived from SUM of shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity for that variant, subtracting any pending order holds).

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate.description:
A single item to purchase within a new order.

Identifies a specific product variant by its unique identifier and the desired quantity. Each entry in the order's items array becomes an individual order item with its own lifecycle status, starting as "paid" after successful payment processing.

The system validates stock availability for every requested variant before processing. The unit price is computed server-side from the variant's current price at checkout — the client must not submit a price. On successful payment, the system atomically creates the order item, captures product, variant, and seller snapshots, deducts inventory, and removes the purchased items from the customer's cart.
IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping for user-provided fields: quantity → shopping_mall_order_items.quantity (positive integer, min 1). Reference: variant_id → shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_product_variant_id (BELONGS-TO FK to shopping_mall_product_variants.id). The variant must exist, not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL), and have sufficient stock (derived from SUM of shopping_mall_inventory_records.quantity for that variant).

Excluded from ICreate: id (auto-generated UUID on creation), shopping_mall_order_id (parent context from the wrapping IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate), price (server-computed from variant's current price or product base price at checkout — client must never submit a price), status (always 'paid' on order creation, set server-side), shopping_mall_shipment_id (assigned later during shipment creation), created_at and updated_at (system-managed timestamps). All belongs-to relations (order, productVariant, shipment) and has-many/has-one relations (cancellationRequests, refundRequests, productSnapshot, variantSnapshot, sellerSnapshot, reviews) are server-managed or belong to different lifecycle stages and are excluded from this DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product snapshot record.

The primary key, automatically generated as a UUID when the snapshot is created at order placement time. This identifier is immutable and serves as the canonical reference for retrieving the full snapshot.

name.description:
Product name as it appeared at the time of order placement.

Preserved verbatim from the original product regardless of later edits, ensuring historical accuracy in order records. This is the display name the customer saw when making the purchase.

description.description:
Product description as it appeared at the time of order placement.

Captures the full descriptive text from the original product at purchase time. Preserved for historical accuracy even if the seller later updates or removes the product description.

basePrice.description:
Base price of the product at the time of order placement.

Preserved in the original currency unit. This is the product-level base price, distinct from the variant-specific price recorded in the variant snapshot. Frozen at order time and never updated, it provides the authoritative price reference for historical order display.

categoryName.description:
Denormalized category name at the time of order placement.

Preserved for historical accuracy even if the referenced category is later renamed, restructured, or deleted by administrators. Provides a direct human-readable category label without requiring a join to the categories table.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

Corresponds to the order creation time. Immutable — set once at order placement and never changed. All snapshot data reflects the product state at this exact point in time.

IShoppingMallOrderItemProductSnapshot.IS.description:
Summary representation of an order item product snapshot for display in nested contexts.

Captures the essential frozen product data — name, description, base price, and category name — as they existed at the moment of order placement. This summary provides a lightweight reference to the product snapshot without including the full image gallery or back-references to original entities.

Each field is preserved verbatim from the original product at purchase time and is immutable. Even if the seller later modifies or deletes the original product, this summary remains an authoritative historical record of what the customer saw when placing the order.
IShoppingMallOrderItemProductSnapshot.IS.x-autobe-specification: Summary view of the product snapshot captured at order placement time. Direct mappings: id from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.id (UUID primary key), name from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.name (frozen product name), description from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.description (frozen product description), basePrice from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.base_price (Float/DoublePrecision, frozen at order time), categoryName from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.category_name (denormalized category name for historical accuracy even if the original category is later renamed or deleted), createdAt from shopping_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ, immutable, set once at order placement). Excluded: productSnapshotImages (HAS-MANY composition), product and category (nullable BELONGS-TO to original entities — denormalized fields suffice for summary context). All fields required — the snapshot is created atomically at order placement with every field populated.

text: Now let me execute the **test agent** to generate comprehensive E2E test suites. I'm extracting all validation rules, business logic workflows, and test-relevant scenarios from your requirements.

instruction:
# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform - E2E Test Requirements

## Account & Authentication Tests
- Registration requires email and password
- Login requires email and password
- Password change workflow
- Account deletion: profile info deleted, orders preserved, reviews preserved as "deleted user"
- Seller registration requires admin approval before selling
- Seller approval status tracking (pending, approved, rejected)
- Rejected sellers can view rejection reason and submit new registration
- Seller deletion blocked if pending orders (paid/shipped) exist
- Seller deletion blocked if pending cancellation/refund requests exist
- Seller deletion: products deleted from listings, order history preserved, shop name preserved

## Profile Tests
- Customer profile: display name and phone number, editable
- Seller profile: shop name, description, logo image, every edit creates snapshot
- Seller profile viewable by customers

## Address Tests
- Multiple shipping addresses per customer
- Address fields: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Edit and delete addresses
- Set default shipping address
- Order address cannot be changed after placement

## Category Tests
- Admin-only CRUD for categories
- One level of subcategory nesting
- Customer browsing of categories
- Viewing products within a category

## Product Tests
- Sellers create products: name, description, category, base price all required
- Product belongs to creating seller
- Every edit creates snapshot (product snapshot includes all fields + variant snapshots)
- Product deletion blocked if pending order items (paid/shipped) for any variant
- Product deletion blocked if pending cancellation/refund requests for any variant
- Product deletion cascades to variants and inventory
- Deleted products hidden from search/listing
- Snapshots preserved after deletion
- Product with no variants: visible but shown as "unavailable"
- Product must have at least one variant to be purchasable

## Product Image Tests
- Multiple images per product, reorderable, deletable
- Image changes included in snapshots

## Variant (SKU) Tests
- SKU code unique identifier required
- Option values, price (optional override), stock quantity (starts at 0)
- Add, edit, delete variants
- Every edit creates snapshot
- Variant deletion blocked if pending orders or cancellation/refund requests

## Inventory Tests
- Stock managed via inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Positive quantity = restock, negative = orders/adjustments
- Current stock = sum of all inventory records
- Restock and adjustment with reason
- Order placement creates negative inventory record automatically
- Cancellation/refund creates positive inventory record automatically
- Stock reaches 0 → "out of stock", cannot add to cart
- Full inventory history viewable per variant

## Search Tests
- Search by name, results from all sellers, paginated
- Filter by: category, price range (min/max), in-stock only
- Sort by: newest first, price low-to-high, price high-to-low
- Listing shows: thumbnail, name, price range, seller shop name, average rating
- Suspended seller products hidden from search/listing

## Wishlist Tests
- Add/remove products (not variants) to wishlist
- Paginated wishlist view
- Deleted product auto-removed from all wishlists

## Cart Tests
- Add variant with quantity, combine quantities for same variant
- View cart: product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal, total
- Change quantity, remove items
- Stock warning if quantity exceeds available stock
- Unavailable marking if variant deleted or out of stock

## Checkout & Order Tests
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Must select shipping address (or use default)
- Order summary review before placement
- Payment success: order created, stock decreased, cart cleared, order items with "paid" status
- Payment failure: order not created, can retry
- Order item snapshot preserves product, variant, and seller profile at purchase time
- Items from different sellers in same order

## Order Status Tests
- Item statuses: Paid → Shipped → Delivered / Cancelled / Refunded
- Order status derived: all paid → "paid", any shipped → "shipped", all delivered → "delivered", all cancelled → "cancelled", all refunded → "refunded", mixed → "partially completed"
- Order history paginated, sorted newest first
- Full order detail: items with status, shipping address, shipments with tracking

## Shipping Tests
- Shipment contains one or more items from same seller
- Different sellers ship separately
- Seller selects items for shipment, enters carrier + tracking number
- All items in shipment get same tracking info
- Items change to "shipped" on shipment creation
- Customer confirms delivery per shipment → items become "delivered"
- Auto-delivery after 14 days without confirmation

## Cancellation Tests
- Per-item cancellation for "paid" items only
- Cancel request includes reason
- Seller approves → item cancelled, refunded, stock restored via inventory record
- Seller rejects → item continues normally
- Response creates snapshot
- All items cancelled → order status "cancelled"
- Remaining items continue processing

## Refund Tests
- Per-item refund for "delivered" items only
- Must be within 7 days of delivery
- Refund request includes reason
- Seller approves → item refunded, stock restored via inventory record
- Seller rejects → item status unchanged
- Response creates snapshot
- All items refunded → order status "refunded"

## Review Tests
- Review only after item delivered
- One review per product per order
- Rating 1-5 required, text optional
- Sorted newest first on product detail page
- Edit creates snapshot, delete preserves snapshot
- Average rating from non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard Tests
- Summary: total products, total order items, pending cancellations, pending refunds
- Order items list filterable by status

## Administrator Tests
- Two grades: regular admin and super admin
- Super admin can promote/demote other admins (cannot demote self)
- Admin request submission with reason, super admin approval/rejection
- Seller approval: view pending, approve, reject with reason
- Suspend seller: products hidden, cannot be purchased, can process existing orders, cannot create/edit products
- Unsuspend seller: products visible again
- Admin CRUD for categories
- View all products, any product snapshots, delete any product
- View all orders, force-cancel items/orders, force-refund items/orders
- View all customers, ban/unban customers
- View all sellers, ban/unban sellers
- Banned users cannot log in
- Banned sellers: existing orders remain

scenario.draft: First-time guest visitor registers via device fingerprint. Submit a join request with a unique device_fingerprint that has never been seen on the platform, along with session context fields (ip, href, referrer). Verify the response returns IShoppingMallGuest.IAuthorized containing: a new UUID guest id, the submitted device_fingerprint, a sessions array with exactly one session record (the newly created session with ip, href, referrer, created_at, and future expired_at), created_at and updated_at timestamps set to now, deleted_at as null, and a valid IAuthorizationToken with access and refresh tokens plus expiration metadata (expired_at ~15 minutes, refreshable_until ~24 hours). Verify the access token can be used as a Bearer token for subsequent authenticated requests.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /shoppingMall/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_first_time

scenario.draft: Returning guest visitor identified by the same device fingerprint. The test pre-condition is that a guest record already exists in the database with a known device_fingerprint and one prior session — achieved by calling join twice with the same fingerprint within the same test. Submit a second join request with that same device_fingerprint. Verify the response reuses the existing guest record: same guest id and device_fingerprint as the prior registration. The sessions array should now contain two session records — the original session and the newly created session — demonstrating the append-only audit trail pattern. Verify that created_at remains the original creation time while updated_at reflects the new session time. Verify token pair is freshly issued with new expiration timestamps.

The test pre-condition is that a soft-deleted guest record exists in the database with a known device_fingerprint and a non-null deleted_at timestamp. Submit a join request with that same device_fingerprint. Verify the system treats it as a brand-new registration: a new UUID guest id is assigned (different from the soft-deleted record's id), a fresh created_at timestamp, deleted_at is null, and exactly one new session is created. The previously soft-deleted record must not be reused or resurrected — this validates the business rule that soft-deleted guests are treated as not found and a fresh record is created.

scenario.draft: Test the successful guest token refresh flow. First, a guest registers via the join endpoint to obtain an initial JWT token pair with a valid refresh token. Then, the guest calls the refresh endpoint with the refresh token, updated session context (IP address, current page URL, and referrer), and verifies: (1) the response returns a 200 status with IShoppingMallGuest.IAuthorized containing a new access token, new refresh token, guest ID, and expiration timestamps; (2) the new access and refresh tokens differ from the original tokens (token rotation); (3) a new session record was created in the database (append-only pattern) with the updated IP, href, and referrer values; (4) the original session remains preserved unchanged in the session history. This validates session continuity for guests navigating between login and registration pages without re-identifying via device fingerprint.

scenario.draft: Test the guest token refresh failure scenario when the refresh token is expired, invalid, or the associated session has expired in the database. First, a guest registers via the join endpoint to obtain an initial token pair. Then, the guest calls the refresh endpoint with a refresh token that has been tampered with, is expired, or belongs to a session whose expired_at has passed. Verify: (1) the response returns a 401 Unauthorized status — the system rejects the refresh when the credential cannot be validated; (2) no new session is created in the database; (3) the guest must re-establish identity through the join endpoint to continue. This validates the security boundary that prevents unauthorized session extension and enforces the explicit session expiration policy where DB-level session expiry overrides JWT validity.

scenario.draft:
Test successful customer registration using only the required fields: a unique email address, a password, a display name, the originating page URL (href), and the HTTP referrer. Do not include the optional phone_number field.

Verify the response returns HTTP 201 (or 200) with the IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized structure containing:
- id: a valid UUID v4 string, non-empty
- email: exactly matching the submitted email address
- display_name: exactly matching the submitted display name
- phone_number: null (since omitted in the request)
- banned_at: null (new accounts are not banned)
- created_at: ISO 8601 timestamp set to the current time (account creation moment)
- updated_at: ISO 8601 timestamp equal to created_at (no modifications yet)
- deleted_at: null (account is active)
- token.access: a non-empty JWT access token string
- token.refresh: a non-empty JWT refresh token string, different from the access token
- token.expired_at: ISO 8601 timestamp approximately 15 minutes after created_at
- token.refreshable_until: ISO 8601 timestamp approximately 7 days after created_at

Confirm the password is never returned in the response. The registration establishes an immediate authenticated session, and a verification email is sent to the provided email address.

scenario.draft:
Test the email uniqueness business rule: a customer cannot register with an email address already in use by an active (non-deleted) customer account.

scenario.draft:
Register a new seller account with complete, valid credentials and verify the full response structure returned upon successful registration.

Steps:
1. Prepare a request body with a unique RFC 5322 email address, a password of at least 8 characters, a valid href URL (the page where registration was initiated, e.g., "https://shop.example.com/seller/register"), a referrer URL (the previous page, e.g., "https://shop.example.com/"), and optionally an IPv4 client IP address (e.g., "192.168.1.100").
2. Send a POST request to /shoppingMall/auth/seller/join.
3. Verify the HTTP response status is 201 Created.
4. Verify the response body contains:
   - id: a non-empty UUID v4 string
   - email: exactly the submitted email address
   - approval_status: exactly "pending" (new sellers await administrator review)
   - rejection_reason: null (no rejection has occurred)
   - suspended_at: null (not suspended)
   - banned_at: null (not banned)
   - created_at: a valid ISO 8601 date-time string
   - updated_at: a valid ISO 8601 date-time string, equal to created_at or very close
   - deleted_at: null (account is active, not soft-deleted)
5. Verify the nested profile object is present with:
   - id: a non-empty UUID v4 string (different from the seller id)
   - shop_name: null (seller has not yet configured a shop name)
   - shop_description: null
   - logo_image_uri: null
   - The profile's created_at and updated_at timestamps should be close to the seller account's created_at
6. Verify the nested token object contains:
   - access: a non-empty JWT string
   - refresh: a non-empty JWT string, distinct from the access token
   - expired_at: a future ISO 8601 date-time (access token expiry)
   - refreshable_until: a future ISO 8601 date-time extending beyond expired_at

scenario.draft:
Verify that an authenticated seller can successfully retrieve a single immutable snapshot of their own seller profile by its unique snapshot ID.

Precondition: The seller has previously edited their shop name, shop description, or logo image, which automatically triggered the creation of an immutable snapshot recording the profile state before the edit was applied. The snapshot ID is known from a prior snapshot listing.

Test steps:
1. Authenticate as the seller via /auth/seller/join to obtain JWT tokens.
2. Call GET /shoppingMall/seller/profile/snapshots/{snapshotId} with a valid snapshot ID belonging to the authenticated seller's own profile.
3. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 with the full IShoppingMallSellerProfileSnapshot object.

Validation points:
- Response includes all required fields: id (UUID), sellerProfile (summary reference to the seller's own profile), shop_name (frozen string from before the edit), shop_description (frozen string), logo_image (frozen URI or null if no logo was set), and created_at (ISO 8601 timestamp).
- The shop_name, shop_description, and logo_image values are immutable frozen copies — they reflect the profile state at the moment before the triggering edit, regardless of subsequent profile changes.
- The sellerProfile reference resolves to the authenticated seller's own profile, confirming ownership scoping.
- If the snapshot's parent seller profile has since been deleted, the snapshot is still returned intact — snapshots outlive profile deletion (Section 449, 571).
- If a non-existent snapshotId is provided, the endpoint returns 404 Not Found.

scenario.draft:
Verify that a seller is denied access when attempting to retrieve another seller's profile snapshot — the system must enforce strict ownership-based authorization and return 403 Forbidden.

Precondition: Seller A has a profile snapshot from a previous profile edit. Seller B is a separate, unrelated seller on the platform.

Test steps:
1. Register and authenticate as Seller A via /auth/seller/join. Seller A edits their profile to trigger automatic snapshot creation. Record the resulting snapshot ID.
2. Register and authenticate as Seller B via /auth/seller/join using different credentials.
3. As Seller B, call GET /shoppingMall/seller/profile/snapshots/{snapshotId} using the snapshot ID that belongs to Seller A's profile.
4. Verify the response returns HTTP 403 Forbidden — the snapshot exists but the requesting seller is not its owner.

Validation points:
- Response status is exactly 403 Forbidden, confirming authorization is enforced at the ownership level.
- No snapshot data is leaked in the response body — seller profile information is properly isolated between tenants.
- After receiving the 403, Seller A can still successfully retrieve the same snapshot with their own token, confirming the snapshot remains intact and authorization is correctly scoped rather than the snapshot being inaccessible.

Business rule reference: Section 450 — "IF a seller requests to view another seller's seller profile snapshot, THEN THE shoppingMall SHALL reject the request." Section 572 — sellers may only view snapshots of their own seller profile.

scenario.draft:
Verify that an administrator can retrieve any seller's profile snapshot on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes, regardless of ownership.

Precondition: A seller has edited their profile, triggering automatic snapshot creation. An administrator account exists with platform-wide snapshot viewing privileges.

Test steps:
1. Register and authenticate as a seller via /auth/seller/join. The seller edits their profile to trigger automatic snapshot creation. Record the snapshot ID.
2. Register and authenticate as an administrator via /auth/admin/join to obtain admin-scoped JWT tokens.
3. As the administrator, call GET /shoppingMall/seller/profile/snapshots/{snapshotId} using the snapshot ID belonging to the seller from step 1.
4. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 with the full IShoppingMallSellerProfileSnapshot object.

Validation points:
- The administrator receives the complete snapshot including the seller's frozen shop_name, shop_description, logo_image (or null), and created_at timestamp — identical in structure to what the owning seller would see.
- The sellerProfile reference within the snapshot correctly links to the seller's profile, even though the requesting actor is an administrator, not the seller.
- The snapshot data is immutable and matches what was recorded at creation time — administrators have read-only access and cannot modify snapshots (Section 571).
- If the seller's profile or account has since been deleted, the snapshot is still returned — confirming that admin access to snapshots survives entity deletion for dispute resolution (Section 449, 572).

Business rule references: Section 192 — administrators may view snapshots of any seller profile. Section 450 — authorized administrator access to any snapshot. Section 572 — administrators can view all snapshots for dispute resolution.

scenario.draft:
Validate that a seller can reorder an image within their product's gallery by moving it to position 0, promoting it to the main thumbnail and causing all intermediate images to shift forward.

Setup: Upload 3 images to the product (display orders 0, 1, 2).

Test: Send a PUT request targeting the image at position 2, setting display_order to 0.

Expected behavior:
- The image's display_order is updated from 2 to 0.
- The image becomes the new main thumbnail — it now occupies the lowest display_order position.
- The previous images at positions 0 and 1 are shifted forward to positions 1 and 2 respectively.
- All display_order values across the product's images are normalized to sequential ordering (0, 1, 2) with no gaps.
- A full product snapshot is created capturing the complete pre-change gallery state — every image's URL and display_order as they existed before this reorder.
- The response body includes the updated image record: id, shopping_mall_product_id, image_url, display_order (0), created_at, and updated_at (reflecting the modification time).

scenario.draft:
Validate that a seller can replace an existing product image file by updating its image_url while preserving its display_order position in the gallery and its identity within existing snapshots.

Setup: Upload a single image to the product (display order 0, serving as main thumbnail).

Test: Send a PUT request updating only the image_url field to a new image file URL, without providing or changing the display_order.

Expected behavior:
- The image_url is updated to the new URL value.
- The display_order remains unchanged at 0 — the image retains its gallery position.
- The image continues to serve as the main thumbnail because it stays at position 0.
- A full product snapshot is created capturing the complete pre-change gallery state (all image URLs and their display orders) before the image URL replacement was applied.
- The image maintains its identity within existing snapshots — the replacement does not orphan or invalidate historical snapshot records.
- The updated_at timestamp reflects the time of modification.
- The response includes the updated image record: id, shopping_mall_product_id, new image_url, display_order (0), created_at, and updated_at.

scenario.draft:
Validate that updating both display_order and image_url in a single request applies both changes correctly and creates exactly one product snapshot — not two.

Setup: Upload 2 images to the product (display orders 0 and 1).

Test: Send a PUT request targeting the image at position 1, providing both a new image_url and display_order set to 0 in the same request body.

Expected behavior:
- Both changes are applied atomically: the image_url is updated AND the display_order is changed to 0.
- The image previously at position 0 is shifted forward to position 1 to accommodate the new ordering.
- The updated image becomes the new main thumbnail since it now occupies the lowest display_order position (0).
- Display orders across the product are normalized to sequential 0, 1 with no gaps.
- Exactly ONE product snapshot is created — even though two fields were changed simultaneously, only a single snapshot captures the complete pre-change gallery state (both images' URLs and their display orders).
- The response includes the updated image record with the new image_url, display_order (0), and an updated updated_at timestamp.

scenario.draft: A customer lists variants of a product and applies the stock_status filter to retrieve only in-stock variants. The test requires at least two variants: one with positive initial stock (in-stock) and one with zero initial stock (out-of-stock). The test validates that when stock_status='in_stock' is specified in the request body, only variants with positive derived stock quantity are returned, and variants with zero or negative stock are excluded. The filter must be applied before pagination — the total record count must reflect only the filtered subset. A second request without the stock_status filter validates that all non-deleted variants are returned regardless of stock level.

The test validates that the endpoint returns an empty result set (empty data array, records=0, pages=0 in pagination) rather than a 404 error response. scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer can retrieve the complete details of an active product variant with a price override. The test sets up a full dependency chain: an admin creates a category, a seller creates a product under that category with a base price, creates a variant with option values (e.g., color: Red, size: Large) and a price override (e.g., 29900), and adds an inventory restock record so the variant has positive stock. Then the customer authenticates and requests the variant. The response must include: the variant's UUID id, globally unique SKU code, optionValues array with correct key-value pairs, the variant-specific price as a number (not null), the parent product's base_price for comparison, a positive stock_quantity computed from inventory records, valid created_at/updated_at timestamps, and deleted_at set to null. This validates the core success path for displaying variant details on product pages.

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer receives a 404 error when attempting to retrieve a soft-deleted variant. This tests the business rule that customers can only see active (non-deleted) variants — soft-deleted variants must be hidden from customer view. The test sets up a variant through admin category creation, seller product and variant creation, then the seller soft-deletes the variant. After the customer authenticates, the GET request for the deleted variant must return HTTP 404, confirming that the role-based soft-delete filtering correctly hides deleted variants from customers. This is a business access-control rule, not input validation.

scenario.draft:
Verify that a seller can successfully soft-delete a variant they own, with all deletion side effects executing correctly.

Steps:
1. An administrator authenticates via join and creates a category.
2. The seller authenticates via join and creates a product under that category.
3. The seller creates a variant under the product with a unique SKU code, option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large"), and an initial stock quantity — this triggers automatic inventory record creation.
4. The seller deletes the variant.

Expected behavior:
- The deletion request returns success (200 or 204).
- The variant's deleted_at timestamp is set, marking it as soft-deleted.
- All inventory records belonging to the variant are permanently removed (hard-deleted).
- The variant no longer appears in the product's variant listing.
- If this was the product's last remaining non-deleted variant, the product becomes unpurchasable and is displayed as unavailable.
- Existing variant snapshots remain preserved and accessible for audit purposes.
- The product's other variants (if any) continue to operate normally.

functions.name: test_api_variant_deletion_by_owning_seller

scenario.draft:
Verify that a seller cannot delete a variant belonging to a product owned by a different seller — authorization is enforced at the product ownership level.

Steps:
1. An administrator authenticates via join and creates a category.
2. Seller A authenticates via join, creates a product under the category, and creates a variant under that product.
3. Seller B (a completely different seller) authenticates via a separate join.
4. Seller B attempts to delete Seller A's variant using Seller A's productId and variantId.

Expected behavior:
- The deletion request is rejected with 403 Forbidden.
- The variant remains unchanged — deleted_at is still null, inventory records remain intact.
- The authorization check compares the authenticated seller's ID (Seller B) against the product's owning seller ID (shopping_mall_seller_id, set to Seller A's ID). Since they do not match, access is denied.
- Seller A's product and variant are unaffected by the unauthorized attempt.

scenario.draft:
Verify that variant snapshots created from standalone variant edits can be distinguished from those created as part of product-level edits using the has_parent_snapshot filter.

Setup: Authenticate as a seller via join. Create a product. Create a variant under that product with SKU code and option values.

Trigger product-level snapshot: Edit the product itself (e.g., change product name). Per business rules, this creates a product snapshot that includes nested variant snapshots — these variant snapshots have a parent product snapshot (has_parent_snapshot = true).

Trigger standalone variant snapshot: Edit the variant independently without touching the product (e.g., change the variant's price). This creates a standalone variant snapshot with no parent product snapshot (has_parent_snapshot = false).

Test 1: List all variant snapshots without any filter — both types should appear.

Test 2: List variant snapshots with has_parent_snapshot = true — only the snapshot from the product-level edit should appear.

Test 3: List variant snapshots with has_parent_snapshot = false — only the standalone variant edit snapshot should appear.

Validation:
- Each filtered query returns only snapshots matching the expected has_parent_snapshot condition
- Snapshots are sorted by created_at descending in all cases

scenario.draft:
Verify that variant snapshots remain accessible after the variant itself is deleted, validating the snapshot preservation business rule.

Setup: Authenticate as a seller via join. Create a product. Create a variant with SKU code and option values.

Trigger snapshot: Edit the variant (e.g., change SKU code) to automatically create a variant snapshot capturing the pre-edit state.

Delete variant: Soft-delete the variant using the variant deletion endpoint.

Test: After variant deletion, call the variant snapshot listing endpoint with the product ID and original variant ID.

Validation:
- The snapshot listing endpoint returns a paginated response containing the snapshot created before deletion
- The snapshot record includes the original sku_code, option_values, and price from before the edit
- The snapshot remains fully accessible to the owning seller even though the live variant no longer exists
- This confirms Section 571's rule: "Variant snapshots remain after a variant is deleted" and Section 449's rule: "WHEN a seller deletes a product variant, THE shoppingMall SHALL preserve all variant snapshots for that variant"

scenario.draft:
Test that the order is rejected with a 409 Conflict when one of the requested variants has insufficient stock, validating the atomic all-or-nothing transaction guarantee. An administrator creates a category. A seller creates a product and adds two variants: Variant A with 5 units of stock via an inventory record, and Variant B created without any inventory record so its stock quantity is zero. The customer attempts to place an order containing both variants — 2 units of Variant A (sufficient stock) and 1 unit of Variant B (zero stock).

Verify the response is a 409 Conflict indicating insufficient stock. Verify that no order was created — querying order history returns no new order. Verify that the variant stock levels remain completely unchanged: Variant A still shows 5 units and Variant B still shows 0 units. Verify that no inventory records were created for either variant (no negative deduction entries exist). Verify that no snapshots were created. This validates the critical business rule: if any variant in the order has insufficient stock, the entire order is rejected atomically — stock is not deducted, no order record exists, and the customer can retry after adjusting their order.

functions.name: test_api_admin_order_items_filter_by_status

functions.name: test_api_shipment_create_multiple_items_bundle

scenario.draft:

functions.name: test_api_shipment_create_individual_items

scenario.draft:
Test that the system enforces the cross-seller shipment prohibition: a seller cannot include order items belonging to a different seller in their shipment (business rule from Sections 403 and 541).

Preconditions:
- Two approved sellers (Seller A and Seller B) each have created products with variants that have stock
- A customer has placed a single order containing items from both Seller A and Seller B, all with "paid" status

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as Seller A
2. Attempt to create a shipment that includes both Seller A's own order item AND Seller B's order item by calling POST /shoppingMall/seller/orders/{orderId}/shipments with both order item IDs
3. Verify the system rejects the request with 403 Forbidden, indicating that cross-seller bundling is not permitted
4. Verify that none of the order items have changed status — they remain "paid"
5. Authenticate as Seller A again and create a valid shipment with only Seller A's own order item to confirm Seller A can still ship their own items independently
6. Verify Seller A's item transitions to "shipped" while Seller B's item remains "paid"

functions.name: test_api_admin_order_shipments_list_multi_seller

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator can filter shipments by delivery status, returning only shipments matching the requested state.

Setup: A customer places an order with items from a single seller. The seller creates two shipments. The customer confirms delivery of the first shipment (making it "delivered" with a delivered_at timestamp). The second shipment remains in transit ("pending" with delivered_at null).

The admin sends two separate requests:
1. First request: deliveryStatus set to "pending" in the request body.
2. Second request: deliveryStatus set to "delivered" in the request body.

Validation points for the "pending" filter:
- Only shipments with delivered_at IS NULL are returned.
- The delivered shipment is excluded from results.
- Each returned shipment has deliveryStatus "pending" and delivered_at null.
- Pagination metadata reflects the filtered count, not total shipments.

Validation points for the "delivered" filter:
- Only the shipment with delivered_at IS NOT NULL is returned.
- The pending shipment is excluded.
- The returned shipment has a non-null delivered_at timestamp and deliveryStatus "delivered".

The filter operates correctly alongside cursor-based pagination parameters (pageSize, cursor).

scenario.draft:
Verify that an authenticated seller can list all their own shipments with default pagination and confirm auto-scoping excludes other sellers' shipments.

8. Verify pagination metadata is internally consistent (records >= data.length, pages = ceil(records / limit) when limit > 0).

scenario.draft:
Validate the primary success path: an authenticated customer submits a cancellation request for their own order item that is in "paid" status, and the request is created with "pending" status.

Setup follows the complete purchase flow:
1. An administrator creates a product category.
2. A new seller registers and is approved by the administrator.
3. The approved seller creates a product with a variant and adds initial stock via an inventory record.
4. A new customer registers, then places an order containing that variant — the order item enters "paid" status.

After setup, the customer submits a cancellation request for their order item with a valid reason (e.g., "Changed my mind, no longer need this item").

Validations on the response:
- HTTP 201 or 200 with the created IShoppingMallCancellationRequest
- status is "pending"
- reason matches the submitted text exactly
- orderItem reference resolves to the correct order item (the itemId from the path)
- id is a valid UUID
- created_at and updated_at are present and equal (newly created)
- deleted_at is null
- The order item itself remains in "paid" status — the cancellation request is pending seller review and does not auto-transition the item

scenario.draft:
Verify that variant snapshots are immutable and preserve historical data even after the seller modifies the original variant post-purchase.

Preconditions: A seller has created a product with a variant (SKU: "PHONE-64GB-BLK", option values: "Storage: 64GB, Color: Black", price: 499.00) and added inventory stock. A customer has placed an order for this variant, creating a variant snapshot at purchase time. After the order is placed, the seller edits the variant — changing its SKU to "PHONE-128GB-BLK", updating the price to 599.00, and modifying the option values to "Storage: 128GB, Color: Black".

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as the customer who placed the order.
2. Retrieve the variant snapshot from the order item using its itemId.
3. Assert the snapshot still shows the original SKU code "PHONE-64GB-BLK" — not the updated "PHONE-128GB-BLK".
4. Assert the snapshot still shows the original option_values "Storage: 64GB, Color: Black" — not "Storage: 128GB, Color: Black".
5. Assert the snapshot still shows the original price 499.00 — not 599.00.
6. Assert the created_at timestamp remains unchanged from the order placement time.

This validates snapshot immutability per Section 571 — the order history remains accurate regardless of later seller modifications. The customer always sees exactly what they actually purchased, and no actor (including administrators) can modify snapshots.

scenario.draft:

- Call the target endpoint with the order item UUID extracted from the placed order.
- Use default pagination (page 1, limit 20) and default sort (display_order ascending).

- Pagination metadata is present with current page, limit, total records, and total pages.

scenario.draft:
Verify pagination and sorting behavior when a seller lists product snapshot images for their own order item.

Setup Flow:

- Call the target endpoint with default parameters (page 1, limit 20, no sort specified).
- Verify images are ordered by display_order ascending — the first image has the lowest display_order value, replicating the original gallery arrangement.
- Verify pagination metadata: current=1, limit=20, records=total image count, pages=ceil(records/20).

Test Execution — Page Navigation:
- Call the target endpoint with page=2 and limit=10.
- Verify the response contains the next batch of images continuing from where page 1 ended (no overlap, no gaps).
- Verify pagination metadata reflects page 2 with correct current, records, and pages values.

Test Execution — Alternative Sort (created_at descending):
- Call the target endpoint with sort=created_at.desc and page=1.

- Use the cursor value from the response to fetch the next page.
- Verify stable iteration through the full result set without duplicates or gaps across cursor boundaries.

- All responses return HTTP 200 with proper ISummary data.
- Pagination metadata is accurate and consistent across all pages.
- Sort order matches the requested sort parameter exactly.
- The frozen snapshot images remain immutable and unchanged throughout all pagination and sorting operations — the same set of image URLs and display_order values appear regardless of navigation method.

scenario.draft: An authenticated seller attempts to access a snapshot image belonging to another seller's order item. Seller B then joins and attempts to GET the snapshot image using Seller A's order item ID and a valid image ID from that snapshot. The request returns 404 Not Found because the specification enforces a chain verification: the snapshot image must belong to a product snapshot whose order item belongs to the requesting seller. scenario.draft:
Verify that a new image record can be added to the frozen product snapshot of an order item, serving as the main thumbnail when placed at display_order 0.

Test Flow:
1. An administrator registers and creates a product category.
2. A seller registers, and the administrator approves the seller.
3. The approved seller creates a product under the category with a base price.
4. The seller creates a variant with SKU code and option values, then adds initial stock via an inventory record.
5. A customer registers and places an order for that variant, which atomically creates the order item and its product snapshot capturing the complete product state at purchase time.
6. Using the order item ID, add a new snapshot image with a valid image_url and display_order of 0.

Validation Points:
- Response returns the created IShoppingMallOrderItemProductSnapshotImage with a server-generated UUID id, the submitted image_url, display_order of 0, and a created_at timestamp.

- Display order 0 is the lowest allowed value (non-negative integer), making this image serve as the main thumbnail — consistent with the rule that the image with the lowest display order is the thumbnail.
- The image record becomes part of the immutable snapshot and persists indefinitely, providing an authoritative historical reference even if the seller later modifies or deletes the original product's live image gallery.

scenario.draft:

scenario.draft:
Apply multiple search filters simultaneously — category, price range, in-stock only, and sort — and validate that only products matching ALL criteria are returned.

Steps:
1. Authenticate as a customer via join.
2. Call the search endpoint with the following combined filters:
   - category_id: a known category UUID (products in this category and its direct subcategories should appear)
   - min_price: a minimum base price threshold
   - max_price: a maximum base price threshold
   - in_stock_only: true
   - sort: 'price_asc'
   - page: 1, limit: 10
3. Validate the response.

Validation points:
- Every product in the result has base_price between min_price and max_price (inclusive).
- Every product has is_purchasable set to true (since in_stock_only filter is active).
- Products without any variants (is_purchasable=false) are excluded when in_stock_only is true.
- Results are sorted by base_price ascending.
- Products from suspended or banned sellers are never included.
- Soft-deleted products are never included.
- The total count in pagination reflects only products matching all combined filters, not the unfiltered total.

instruction:
# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform - Implementation Requirements

## Account & Authentication
- Password must be securely hashed (bcrypt)
- JWT-based authentication with access token and refresh token
- Account deletion for customers: soft-delete profile, preserve orders and order history, preserve reviews but mark as "deleted user"
- Account deletion for sellers: blocked if pending orders (paid/shipped) or pending cancellation/refund requests exist; on deletion, soft-delete products, preserve order history and snapshots, preserve shop name in past orders
- Seller registration: status "pending" by default, requires admin approval
- Seller approval status visible to seller: pending, approved (with approved_at), rejected (with rejection_reason)
- Rejected sellers can resubmit: creates new registration request
- Banned users (customer or seller) cannot log in — return 403 Forbidden with appropriate message

## Profile Management
- Customer profile: display_name (required), phone_number (required)
- Seller profile: shop_name (required), shop_description (required), logo_image (optional)
- Every seller profile edit creates a SellerProfileSnapshot with: changed_fields JSON, before_values JSON, after_values JSON, created_at timestamp

## Address Management
- One default address per customer enforced at application level
- When setting a new default, unset previous default

## Category Management
- One level of nesting enforced: parent_id can only reference categories where parent_id IS NULL
- Admin-only operations validated by role check
- Deleting a category: products in that category become uncategorized (category_id set to null)

## Snapshot System
- Immutable: snapshots cannot be updated or deleted
- Product snapshot: captures all product fields (name, description, category_id, base_price) + all image URLs at that moment + all variant snapshots at that moment
- Product variant snapshot: captures sku_code, option_values JSON, price
- Seller profile snapshot: captures shop_name, shop_description, logo_image
- Order item snapshot: captures product snapshot, variant snapshot, and seller profile snapshot at time of purchase
- Review snapshot: captures rating, content
- Cancellation/refund request snapshot: captures reason, status change, responded_by, responded_at
- changed_fields stored as JSON array of field names
- before_values and after_values stored as JSON objects mapping field name → value

## Inventory Management
- Stock calculated as SUM of all inventory record quantity_change values for a variant
- Order placement: create inventory record with -quantity for each variant, reason: "order_{orderId}"
- Order cancellation (approved): create inventory record with +quantity, reason: "cancellation_{cancellationId}"
- Order refund (approved): create inventory record with +quantity, reason: "refund_{refundId}"
- Admin force-cancel/refund: same inventory restoration logic
- Variant displayed as "out of stock" when calculated stock <= 0
- Adding to cart: validate stock >= requested quantity, reject if insufficient

## Cart Logic
- Add to cart: if same variant exists, ADD quantities (quantity = existing + new), not separate line
- Cart item subtotal = variant price * quantity
- Cart total = SUM of all item subtotals
- Stock validation: if current stock < cart quantity, return warning flag per item
- Unavailable marking: if variant deleted or stock <= 0, mark item with unavailable flag
- Checkout: only process items that are available (in stock, variant exists, product exists, seller not suspended)
- On successful order: clear cart items that were ordered

## Order Creation
- Transaction: create order, create order items with status "paid", create inventory records (negative), clear cart items, create order item snapshots
- Order item snapshot includes: product snapshot (all fields + images), variant snapshot (SKU + options + price), seller profile snapshot (shop_name + logo_image)
- Payment simulation: assume external gateway; implement with success/failure response pattern
- On payment failure: rollback transaction, return error with retry capability
- Order number: auto-generated sequential format like "ORD-{YYYYMMDD}-{sequential}"
- Shipping address captured at order level and immutable after placement

## Order Status Derivation
- Compute order status dynamically from items:
  - All items "paid" → order "paid"
  - Any item "shipped" and none "delivered" → order "shipped"
  - All items "delivered" → order "delivered"
  - All items "cancelled" → order "cancelled"
  - All items "refunded" → order "refunded"
  - Mixed states → order "partially_completed"

## Shipping Logic
- Shipment validation: all items must belong to same seller, all items must be in "paid" status
- On shipment creation: all included items change to "shipped" status, shipment gets created_at timestamp
- Tracking info: carrier_name and tracking_number required
- Delivery confirmation: customer confirms → all items in shipment change to "delivered" with delivered_at timestamp
- Auto-delivery: background job or check on order view — if shipped_at + 14 days < now and status is "shipped", auto-set to "delivered"
- Different sellers = always separate shipments (enforced at app level)

## Cancellation Logic
- Validate: item status must be "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Customer submits: reason text, status "pending"
- Seller approves: item status → "cancelled", create inventory record (+quantity, reason: "cancellation_{id}"), process refund for that item
- Seller rejects: status "rejected", item continues processing normally
- On seller response: create snapshot of cancellation request (reason, status, responded_by, responded_at)

## Refund Logic
- Validate: item status must be "delivered", request within 7 days of delivered_at
- Customer submits: reason text, status "pending"
- Seller approves: item status → "refunded", create inventory record (+quantity, reason: "refund_{id}"), process refund
- Seller rejects: status "rejected", item status unchanged
- On seller response: create snapshot of refund request

## Review Logic
- Validate: item must be "delivered", customer must have purchased this product in this order
- One review per product per order (unique constraint on customer_id + product_id + order_id)
- Rating: 1-5 integer
- Edit: creates ReviewSnapshot with changed fields and before/after values
- Delete: soft-delete review (is_deleted flag), preserve snapshots
- Average rating: AVG of rating from all non-deleted reviews for a product

## Admin Operations
- Role hierarchy: super_admin > admin > user
- Super admin can promote admin → super_admin
- Super admin can demote super_admin → admin (not self)
- Admin request: any user submits with reason, super admin approves/rejects
- Seller approval: admin approves (status → "approved", approved_at set) or rejects (status → "rejected", rejection_reason set)
- Suspend seller: set is_suspended flag; on suspension: hide products from search/listing, block purchases, allow existing order processing, block product CRUD
- Unsuspend: clear is_suspended flag, products visible again
- Force-cancel: admin cancels any item/order, same as regular cancellation but with admin actor recorded
- Force-refund: admin refunds any item/order, same as regular refund but with admin actor recorded
- Ban customer: set is_banned flag, prevent login
- Ban seller: set is_banned flag, prevent login, existing orders remain unaffected
- Unban: clear is_banned flag

## Search Logic
- Search by name: WHERE name ILIKE '%query%' AND is_deleted = false AND seller.is_suspended = false
- Filter by category: WHERE category_id = ? (include subcategories if parent category selected)
- Filter by price range: WHERE base_price BETWEEN min AND max (or variant prices)
- Filter in-stock only: only products with at least one variant having stock > 0
- Sort: ORDER BY created_at DESC (newest), price ASC, price DESC
- Price range display: if all variants same price → show single price; if different → show "min - max"
- Average rating included in listing

## Seller Dashboard
- Total products: COUNT of seller's non-deleted products
- Total order items: COUNT of order items for seller's products
- Pending cancellations: COUNT of cancellation requests with status "pending" for seller's products
- Pending refunds: COUNT of refund requests with status "pending" for seller's products
- Order items list: filterable by status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)

## Data Integrity
- All monetary values stored as integers (cents) to avoid floating point issues
- All timestamps in UTC
- Soft delete pattern where specified (products, reviews)
- Snapshot immutability enforced (no UPDATE or DELETE on snapshot tables)
- Cascading logic implemented at application level for complex rules
